Company size and individual executive actions influence Responsible AI (RAI) prioritization in several ways. Larger companies may have the resources to offer training sessions to existing employees about RAI topics, which can enhance awareness and integration of RAI practices. In contrast, smaller companies might have a more unified leadership that can quickly align on RAI priorities.

Individual executive actions play a crucial role as well; executives with sufficient power can champion RAI initiatives, especially in hierarchical or smaller organizations where leadership is unified. However, individual circumstances can also lead to deprioritization of RAI if executives fear setting precedents or if past RAI efforts did not yield positive results. Thus, while company size can provide structural advantages for RAI prioritization, the actions and motivations of individual executives are critical in determining the actual prioritization of RAI within the organization.
